## Observation
A local `make verify` (worktree w1-koala-goose, test-only change to test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py; host running 3 concurrent verifies, wall time 1:49:19) failed `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_store.py::test_in_flight_refusal_clears_owned_pause_before_mutation[doctor]`: `RefLockTimeoutError: git update-ref refs/reconciler/gate timed out after 5.0s (fail-closed: treat as HELD)`, re-raised as `RepairPauseError: a reconciler pass is in flight`. The suite had 1 failed, 21561 passed. The module then passed 3 times in isolation on the same host (30 passed each, 58 s, 131 s, 135 s).

## Hypothesis (unproven)
Same class as closed ticket sensible-curt-acouchi: the test fails whenever one local `git update-ref` in its temp repo exceeds `_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (5.0 s), which host load can cause. Not yet reproduced deterministically with a delaying git shim for this test.

## Root cause (reproduced deterministically on 2026-11-19)
The hypothesis holds. A PATH shim (`git` wrapper that sleeps before any `update-ref`, then runs the real git) on origin/main 2ca3e28fcc6:
- delay 4.5 s: `test_in_flight_refusal_clears_owned_pause_before_mutation` 2 passed.
- delay 5.6 s: both parameters fail. `[doctor]` raises `RefLockTimeoutError: git update-ref refs/reconciler/gate timed out after 5.0s (fail-closed: treat as HELD)` from `set_pause`, re-raised as `RepairPauseError: Error: doctor repair could not acquire its reconciliation pause`; `[fsck]` reports the same refusal. In the reported run the slow call was the cleanup delete of the same ref, which takes the same path.
The test asserts pause-ownership semantics but runs real git in a temporary repository under the production bound `_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 5.0`, which it does not control. The production behaviour is correct: a local ref operation that takes over 5 s is treated as HELD (fail-closed, ADR policy), and closed bugs sensible-curt-acouchi and dissocial-malleable-tuna kept that bound.

## The class
This is the third module to fail this way. sensible-curt-acouchi fixed `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py` and dissocial-malleable-tuna fixed `tests/interfaces/store/test_bridge_sync_holds_ref_lock.py`, each with a per-module `monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, "_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS", 60.0)`. 35 test files drive the ref-lock backend; each one that runs real git is exposed until someone adds the same line after a CI failure.

## Approach
Set the bound once for the test session instead of per module. In `tests/conftest.py`'s `pytest_configure`, set `rebar.reconciler._ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 60.0` (xdist workers run `pytest_configure` too). `_ref_lock` is always reached as that one module object (`_advisory_lock._load_ref_lock` is `importlib.import_module("rebar.reconciler._ref_lock")`), and `_ref_lock_push` reads `core._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` at call time, so every in-process caller sees it. Production code is unchanged: the bound stays 5.0 s and a timeout still means HELD. The fail-closed contract stays proven by `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py::test_timeout_raises_reflocktimeout`, which forces `TimeoutExpired` independently of the bound. Remove the two per-module overrides, which the session setting replaces, and point their docstrings at it. This loosens a time bound in test code only; it is recorded here as the prior tickets recorded theirs.
Limit: a rebar child process started by a test does not inherit an in-process setting; this change covers in-process callers only.
Rejected: raising the production bound (it is a deliberate fail-closed policy); another per-module override (the class reopens with the next module).

## Scope
- `tests/conftest.py`
- `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py`
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_bridge_sync_holds_ref_lock.py`
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_store.py`

## Testing
- Add `test_a_slow_local_git_call_does_not_fail_the_repair_pause` to `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_store.py`: with a PATH `git` shim that sleeps 5.6 s before `update-ref` and records each delayed call to a file, run the doctor in-flight path and assert the `a reconciler pass is in flight` refusal, that no pause is left behind, and that the shim recorded at least one delayed `update-ref` (so the test cannot pass without exercising the delay). On the pre-fix tree it fails with the timeout above; with the session setting it passes.
- `test_advisory_lock.py`'s existing slow-git test keeps passing with its module override removed.
- `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py`, `test_ref_lock_blob_read_budget.py` (it compares recorded budgets to the module attribute), `test_advisory_lock.py`, `test_bridge_sync_holds_ref_lock.py`, and `test_repair_pause_ownership_store.py` pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The failure is reproduced deterministically (e.g. a git shim delaying update-ref past 5 s) and the root cause recorded.
- [x] The test no longer fails under that reproduction, or the bug is closed with the evidence-backed disposition.
- [x] The new slow-git test fails on the pre-fix tree and passes with the change (both runs recorded here).
- [x] `make verify` passes on the change.
